content.text:
**The fixes are substantially stronger, but I would not approve PR #8 yet.** Reviewed current head `72a2ae2`, focusing on the latest fixes and migration correctness.

One confirmed remaining finding:

- **[P1] R2 immutable-object protection is still non-atomic.** [`putIfAbsent`](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2F21nCo%2Fskillplane%2Fpull%2F8&path=scripts%2Flib%2Fwrangler-r2-migration-store.mjs&line=113&side=right) checks for an existing object, then performs an unconditional write. Two writers can both observe absence and overwrite each other. I reproduced this with an in-memory interleaving: both returned `created`; the second replaced the first. The fix protects against objects already present when checked, but needs an atomic conditional create to fulfill its contract.

The fixes otherwise show good quality:

| Area | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Migration keys and sequences | Substantive repair with collision handling, foreign-key remapping, sequence locks, and meaningful PostgreSQL regression coverage. |
| Historical migration upgrades | Shared, narrowly scoped hash compatibility and the follow-up trigger migration address the earlier upgrade gaps. |
| Projection backlog | Removes the fixed 100-event ceiling while preserving workspace ordering and failure isolation. Mocked tests verify the budget logic; sustained production throughput remains unproven. |
| Global audit retention | Carries retention classification through storage and adds cleanup. The PostgreSQL test confirms old detailed reads expire while permanent/recent evidence survives. |
| Unknown MCP tools | Correctly delegates to protocol handling. The new routing test uses a stub handler, so it is not full protocol-conformance evidence. |

**Validation:** 68 tests passed across 15 files, including 16 PostgreSQL integration tests. The checkout remains clean; no code was changed. The pnpm wrapper rejected the installed version mismatch, so I ran the installed Vitest executable directly.

The 52 unresolved threads are **not 52 confirmed defects**—several describe repaired code. External gates are also incomplete: GitGuardian fails, SonarCloud is cancelled, and reviewers are still running. CodeRabbit’s green status represents a skipped review because the PR exceeds its file limit.

This was a focused fix-quality review, not a fresh exhaustive audit of the entire PR.

content.text:
**`03fc877` is the strongest overall fix commit; `05200ff` makes the largest substantive improvement; `72a2ae2` is the cleanest small fix round.** Earlier migration fixes were useful but repeatedly incomplete.

Comparing the recent fix chain **as each commit stood when introduced**, rather than crediting it with later repairs:

| Commit | Relative quality | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [`03fc877`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/03fc877) | **Strongest overall** | Closes specific correctness gaps: sequence locking, workspace-scoped foreign-key validation, shared migration-hash verification, and upgrade-trigger reconciliation. Tests exercise actual concurrency and historical upgrades. |
| [`72a2ae2`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/72a2ae2) | **Strong, focused** | Addresses three concrete behaviors with modest changes and targeted tests. Less demanding than migration repair; throughput is tested with a mocked clock, and protocol delegation with a stub. |
| [`05200ff`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/05200ff) | **Strongest substantive advance, incomplete alone** | Replaces verification that ignored remapped keys with full expected-row verification and adds a broad migration matrix. However, `03fc877` still had to repair cross-workspace validation, sequence locking, and verifier compatibility. |
| [`c4d36a3`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/c4d36a3) | **Good narrow correction** | Correctly diagnoses deferred-trigger behavior and avoids transient region disabling. Small, understandable change; no new regression tests in this commit. |
| [`26d2291`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/26d2291) | **Mixed** | Bucket-to-region binding is a good complete fix. Completion recovery initially trusted the journal’s target match without validating the proof against live placement and epoch; required follow-up. |
| [`2f6f627`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/2f6f627) | **Good diagnosis, incomplete upgrade handling** | Adds a realistic populated-upgrade regression and correctly delays FK validation. Editing migration `0043` creates historical-ledger compatibility work that later commits had to handle. |
| [`ff0e0cf`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/ff0e0cf) | **Useful but uneven** | Strengthens recovery evidence and fresh-cell preparation. Its new cleanup migration assumes a table still exists, breaking already-pruned regional databases until repaired. |
| [`ee7e682`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/ee7e682) | **Partial correctness** | Improves schema copying, but preserving cell-local identity values leaves collisions; resetting sequences from table maxima leaves concurrency hazards. |
| [`513d866`](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/commit/513d866) | **Weakest verification approach in this group** | Adds key remapping, but excludes remapped keys and references from checksums—weakening verification precisely where the transformation is risky. `05200ff` substantially replaces that approach. |

The clearest progression is **`513d866` → `05200ff` → `03fc877`**: first handle collisions, then verify the transformed relationships, then close concurrency and workspace-isolation gaps. The latter two show much better reasoning about the complete migration contract.

These are code-quality judgments, not author/model rankings. I inspected historical diffs, but the **68 passing tests were run at the current head**, not independently at each historical commit.

Chronological order, oldest first. Times are **IST**.

| Commit | Timestamp | Relative quality |
|---|---|---|
| `c4d36a3` | Sep 3, 13:53 | **Good narrow correction** — accurate deferred-trigger fix; no new regression tests. |
| `2f6f627` | Sep 3, 15:14 | **Good diagnosis, incomplete upgrade handling** — realistic FK regression; historical migration compatibility needed follow-up. |
| `26d2291` | Sep 3, 19:29 | **Mixed** — solid bucket binding; recovery proof validation incomplete. |
| `ff0e0cf` | Sep 4, 08:55 | **Useful but uneven** — stronger recovery; cleanup migration broke already-pruned databases. |
| `ee7e682` | Sep 5, 12:39 | **Partial correctness** — improved schema copying; identity collisions and sequence races remained. |
| `513d866` | Sep 5, 18:17 | **Weak verification approach** — remapped keys but excluded those keys/references from checksums. |
| `05200ff` | Sep 8, 18:25 | **Largest substantive improvement** — full transformed-row verification and broad tests; some correctness gaps remained. |
| `03fc877` | Sep 8, 20:51 | **Strongest overall** — closes concurrency, workspace-isolation, and historical-upgrade gaps with meaningful tests. |
| `72a2ae2` | Sep 9, 19:50 | **Strong, focused** — clean fixes for throughput, retention, and protocol delegation; limited end-to-end evidence. |
